implementation_notes: There is no tooling that removes it; the evidence is in your change history. Measure: for the last N commits, count files touched and look for the same file set recurring across unrelated requirements — that recurrence is the smell, since a genuinely cross-file feature is rare. The Fowler/Beck recipe when the fragments are functions is: Move Function/Move Field to gather them; if many functions transform the same structure, Combine Functions into Transform; if the shared part produces input for a later consuming phase, Split Phase. When the fragments are classes that are each almost empty after the move, Inline Class them away. The honest alternative for a genuine cross-cutting concern is not a move at all but an aspect/decorator/interceptor that applies once at a boundary.
idiom_name: Move Method/Field + Combine Functions into Class/Transform, or Inline first
pitfalls: Consolidating scattered code into one class that then needs to call back into every fragment produces a cycle.
Counting files per commit will flag genuine large features; the signal is recurrence across unrelated requirements.
Inlining everything first can hand you a Large Class that is equally hard to work with; the sequence matters, the destination is not a small class by construction.
